title: Undead
html:
Undead are a type of creature that has died and been brought back through magical or spiritual means. They are frequently found throughout Baldur's Gate 3, most notably during Act Three, and may be created through various spells and actions available to players and NPCs.

“
Remnants of the once-living that are trapped between life and death.
„
— In-game racial description

Characteristics

Most undead are reanimated from formerly living creatures, and generally exist between the realms of the living and the dead. As such, certain damage types or status effects that would normally be effective against organic creatures are ineffective against undead creatures. ⁠Poison and ⁠Necrotic resistances appear quite commonly, and some are often immune to Poison or Necrotic damage, or both. Similarly, they are unaffected by many conditions such as  Bleeding and  Poisoned.

Conversely, almost all healing effects including  Healing Word,  Lay on Hands, and  Preserve Life have no effect on undead. However, potions can still heal them.[verify]  Aid can heal the undead.

Types of undead

Conjured Spectres

Main articles: Conjured Spectre and  Spectre on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Phantasms of arcane origin.
„
— In-game racial description

Crawling Claw

Main articles: Crawling Claw and  Crawling claw on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Severed from their owners and skittering along on digits still stiff with rigor mortis, these hands can squeeze the breath from a throat in an instant.
„
— In-game racial description

Crawling claw and reanimated severed limbs, usually created to perform menial tasks as a servant by dark wizards. Lacking a brain, crawling claws do not possess intelligence, although they can still hear and understand basic commands.

Crawling claws in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Itchy
  •  Scratchy

Dark Justiciar

Main articles: Dark Justiciar and  Dark Justiciars on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Remnants of the once-living that are trapped between life and death.
„
— In-game racial description

Dark Justiciars are elite warriors who serve Shar, some even after death. Their skeletal remains are in Grymforge during Act One, and all but one serve the Dark Lady as undead in the Gauntlet of Shar in Act Two.

Death Knight

Main articles: Death Knight and  Death knight on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
When a fallen paladin dies without atonement, it can be brought back from the grave as something entirely different - entirely evil.
„
— In-game racial description

Death knights are reanimated warriors, often created from those who were evil in life. They appear fully clad in armour, which hides their rotting skin such that only their eyes show through as pinpoints of light. Death knights were most often created from those who were, or whose behaviors aligned with, paladins or others sufficiently of their ilk.

Death knights in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Stalker Svignee
  •  That Which Guards
  •  That Which Lurks
  •  That Which Watches

Flying Ghoul

Main articles: Flying Ghoul
“
With their jagged wings and razor-sharp teeth, these undead gorge on humanoid flesh in the depth of night.
„
— In-game racial description

Flying Ghouls are flying variants of the regular Ghoul. They have large jagged wings and often swoop down to consume humanoid corpses

Flying ghouls in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Winged Horror

Ghast

Main articles: Ghast and  Ghast on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Orcus, god of undeath, creates ghasts by infusing ghouls with a particularly baleful dosage of his abyssal energy. Whereas a ghoul is little more than a savage beast, a ghast is cunning and can inspire a pack of ghouls to obey its commands.
„
— In-game racial description

Ghasts are very similar to ghouls - humanoid creatures that can paralyze their foes with their claws and teeth. They are generally more cunning and deadly, but carry the stench of rotting flesh. This stench is so severe it can cause  nausea, and even  paralysis.

Ghasts in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Fallen Gur Hunter
  •  Ulnar

Ghost

Main articles: Ghost and  Ghost on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
The soul of a once-living creature, bound to the material plane by its desire to resolve some unfinished task from its life.
„
— In-game racial description

Ghosts are spirits which are bound to someone or some place, either from being denied a proper burial or by having unfinished business when they died. Being incorporeal, they can fly and pass through solid objects as they please.

Ghoul

Main articles: Ghoul and  Ghoul on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Driven by their insatiable hunger for humanoid flesh, ghouls usually roam the night in packs.
„
— In-game racial description

Ghouls are humanoid looking carnivorous creatures that devour corpses and hunger for the flesh of living beings. They have long sharp teeth, and can  paralyze their prey with claw or bite wounds.

Grim Visage

Main articles: Grim Visage and  Grim Visage on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
These skulls spawned from Gerringothe Thorm's twisted psyche. Manifestations of her worst flaws, they keep the coins of her protective armour intact.
„
— In-game racial description

Grim visages are floating skulls created from various aspects of Gerringothe Thorm's personality to guard her coins. There are six of these reprehensible aspects; defeating any of them removes armor from Gerringothe.

Grim Visages in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Visage of Cowardice

Mummy

Main articles: Mummy and  Mummy on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Shambling, their bodies clothed with rotted scraps of funereal wrappings, mummies bring their malice with them out of their tombs.
„
— In-game racial description

Mummies are undead creatures created from preserved, mummified corpses. They retain the bandages which wrapped and preserved their body, but are in various stages of extreme decay. If attacked by a mummy, a condition known as  Mummy Rot may be inflicted.

Mummies in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Ancient Servant
  •  Zara the Mummy

Mummy Lord

Main articles: Mummy Lord and  Mummy lord on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Huddled in their sarcophagi like sickly penitents, mummy lords creep out to protect their tombs, their crumbling rags host to fierce ancient fists and skin crawling with curses.
„
— In-game racial description

Mummy lords are more powerful, intelligent versions of Mummies which are created from powerful creatures. If defeated, they automatically reform in their lair unless their desiccated hearts are found and destroyed by fire.

Mummy Lords in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Mystic Carrion

Shadow

Main articles: Shadow and  Shadow on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Resembling dark exaggerations of humanoid shadows, these undead feed on the vitality of the living creatures they were once part of.
„
— In-game racial description

Shadows are dark, incorporeal creatures. Those found in Act Two are the are twisted remnants of once living creatures who have been corrupted and consumed by the Shadow Curse. When defeated, they usually leave behind a Shadow Vestige; interacting with these reveals fragments of their former lives.

Shadows in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Shadow Friend
  •  Shadow Plush
  •  The Judge

Skeleton

Main articles: Skeleton and  Skeleton on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
The remains of the dead, animated by dark magic - be they summoned by spellcasters, or risen on their own.
„
— In-game racial description

Skeletons are a commonly encountered form of undead. They are animated from a corpse of a creature that is devoid of flesh. Consisting of mainly brittle bones, skeletons are vulnerable to ⁠Bludgeoning damage and can be created through various magic spells.

Undead Dragon

Main article: Undead Dragon
“
Bones studded with rotting scales and draped with dead tissue, these dragons have been animated by fell necromancy.
„
— In-game racial description

Undead dragons are exceedingly rare creatures reanimated by use of extraordinarily powerful magic. Their bodies are skeletal in appearance, and they retain much of their abilities and magic as they had in life.

Undead dragons in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Ansur

Vampire

Main articles: Vampire and  Vampire on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Amiable aristocrats and cold-hearted hunters, vampires are the embodiments of evening made flesh.
„
— In-game racial description

Vampires are powerful undead creatures known for their pale-skin, sharp claws, blood-red eyes, and sharp teeth used to pierce and drink the blood of their victims. They can regenerate, as well as turn other humanoid creatures into vampire spawn by feeding on them. They are also known for their sensitivity to sunlight, and their skin burns in its presence.

Vampires in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Cazador Szarr

Vampire Spawn

Main articles: Vampire Spawn and  Vampire spawn on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Subservient to the one who created them, vampire spawn are deadly hunters both ravenous and proud.
„
— In-game racial description

Vampire spawn are creatures created when a vampire bites and drinks the blood of a humanoid creature and allows it to survive. They have some of the features of a vampire such as sensitivity to light and a hunger for blood, but are bound to the one who turned them unless their master is killed, or their freedom is granted.

Wraith

Main articles: Wraith and  Wraith on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
A wraith is malice incarnate, concentrated into an incorporeal form that seeks to quench all life. Even small fires can be extinguished by the sucking oblivion of the wraith's horrifying existence.
„
— In-game racial description

Wraiths are similar in appearance to Shadows, and can also be found in Act Two. In combat, Wraiths frequently teleport from shadow to shadow. They also generate an  Aura of Vile Oblivion which snuffs out nearby light sources and can drain the life of their enemies.

Wraiths in Baldur's Gate 3

  •  Daddy
  •  Mummy

Zombie

Main articles: Zombie and  Zombie on the Forgotten Realms Wiki
“
Mindless remains of the dead, imbued with necromantic magic, zombies do their creator's bidding without fear or hesitation.
„
— In-game racial description

Zombies are a common form of undead similar to Skeletons except for retaining significant amounts of flesh. Mindless and often missing body parts, zombies can be created from most living creatures and they usually form the backbone of any necromancer's army. Zombies can be resilient opponents, often recovering after receiving an otherwise fatal blow.

Related items

  • Arrow of Undead Slaying - double damage against undead creatures
  • Blade of Oppressed Souls -  Crowning Strike won't apply Crown of Madness to undead
  • Circle of Bones - grants all nearby allied undead Resistance to physical damage
  • Doom Hammer - prevents healing and applies disadvantage to their attacks
  • Gandrel's Aspiration -  Sacred Munitions allows ranged weapon attacks to turn undead
  • Hammer of the Just - additional damage against undead
  • Holy Water - deals 3d6⁠⁠Radiant damage against undead
  • Pelorsun Blade -  Advantage against undead
  • Planeslayer Flail (inaccessible) - bonus damage and attack roll against undead
  • Resonance Stone - does not affect undead
  • Sword of Life Stealing - target takes additional ⁠Necrotic damage unless it is undead
  • The Blood of Lathander - blinds nearby undead creatures
  • The Long Arm of the Gur - bonus to attack and damage against undead
  • The Oak Father's Embrace - deals ⁠Radiant damage to undead creatures that hit the wearer
  • The Sacred Star - turns undead creatures if they fail a saving throw.
  • The Undead Bane - deals additional damage and applies  Bane to undead
  • Veil of the Morning - undead have disadvantage against the wearer, and the wearer has advantage against saving throws from undead creatures

Related spells and abilities

  • Aura of Hate - nearby undead deal Charisma modifier additional damage with weapon attacks
  • Bone Chill - Undead receive disadvantage on attack rolls.
  • Carrion's Explosive Cloudkill - forces an undead corpse to explode, creating a  Cloudkill cloud
  • Claws (Flying Ghoul) - undead are not paralyzed by the attack
  • Control Undead - must be used on undead
  • Crown of Madness - takes control of target undead for a period of time
  • Divine Sense - grants advantage on attack rolls against undead
  • Divine Smite - deals an additional 1d6⁠⁠Radiant to undead
  •  Holy Fire - deals an extra 1d4⁠⁠Radiant damage per turn
  •  Marshal Undead - grants nearby undead resistance to  Turn Undead
  • Mortal Uncoiling - Controls an undead but kills it at the end of battle
  • No Rest for the Wicked - Raises a fallen undead creature with half its hit points
  • Protection from Evil and Good - undead have disadvantage against the target
  •  Sacred Defiance Aura - grants nearby undead resistance to  Turn Undead
  • Turn the Unholy - Forces nearby undead to flee
  • Turn Undead - Forces nearby undead to flee
  •  Undead Ward Aura - allied undead become resistant to ⁠Bludgeoning, ⁠Slashing, and ⁠Piercing damage.
